scenario_notes: Seven people over three days. Three interleaved decisions: end-state platform, cutover timing, interim on-call ownership. Priorities change twice (speed first, then compliance first). Sarcasm, a half-serious option that is dropped then revived as interim only, a poll with an abstention, a chair's bare 'ok', a reply-linked '+1', a misattributed stance and a false 'everyone is on board' claim, hearsay that is later corrected, an estimate mistaken for a budget, two sensitive disclosures, off-topic questions, a contract deadline that interacts with the timing decision, and an on-call question that never gets an owner. The platform direction is clear and not formally confirmed.
decision_question: What end-state data platform should we consolidate on after the merger, and when do we cut over?
outcome: Direction, not final: Databricks as the end state, Q2 cutover with the exact date to follow Raj's assessment and the Dec 8 security review, federation only as an interim bridge. Sofia will confirm the platform formally at the Nov 16 steering. Interim on-call is unowned.

executive_summary.title: What end-state data platform should we consolidate on after the merger, and when do we cut over?
executive_summary.status_line: 5 options (2 dropped); Databricks (A): explicit support from Colleen, Imani, Gareth (3); conditional: Raj, Wei; acknowledged only: Dmitri; Federate across both platforms: explicit support from Imani (1); conditional: Colleen, Sofia; Q2 cutover: explicit support from Raj, Imani, Dmitri, Sofia (4); conditional: Gareth; 0 open objections; 4 open blockers; 1 action without a named owner.

needs_attention.text: Snowflake auto-renews for 3 years on Feb 28 unless notice is given by Nov 30. A Q2 cutover lands after Feb 28, so serving notice alone leaves a gap. Dmitri will ask for a 6-month extension to Aug 31 by Nov 20. If refused, a one-year renewal (about $2.4M, his estimate) puts the 10% cost target at risk. The 10% target itself is second-hand.
Interim on-call for the legacy Snowflake pipelines has no owner. Raj's team and Colleen's team each said they cannot take it, Sofia parked it, and Gareth has raised it again since.

Raj's and Wei's support is conditional. Raj: stored-procedure assessment due Nov 6 (9 of 40 need rewrites; effort is disputed, 2 weeks vs 4 to 6). Wei: BAA addendum review due Nov 13 and member-ID tokenization. The security architecture review starts Dec 8 and takes about 3 weeks before any PHI moves.
Support is not unanimous. Colleen's 'all seven on board' was corrected by Wei, Raj and Dmitri. Dmitri abstained in the poll and later only acknowledged ('Fine, whatever').
Priorities changed. Monday's order was speed, cost, compliance; on Tuesday Sofia reordered to compliance, cost, speed. The March target was dropped.

proposed.text: Databricks (A) as the end state: explicit support from Colleen, Imani and Gareth; conditional: Raj (stored procedures) and Wei (BAA, tokenization); Dmitri acknowledged only. Sofia proposed it as the direction. Snowflake (B) was withdrawn by Raj once Halden committed two engineers.

Q2 cutover, with the exact date after Raj's assessment and the Dec 8 review: explicit support from Raj, Imani, Dmitri and Sofia; conditional: Gareth (stored-procedure answer). The March target is dropped.
Federating queries across both platforms: interim bridge only, not an end state. Imani supports it; Colleen and Sofia accept it as temporary.

traps.note: Colleen claims Raj is 'fine' with Databricks. Raj says conditional. Record Raj as conditional, not support.
Gareth's sarcasm ('Totally realistic') is an objection to the March timeline. It is not support for anything.
Federation: half-serious, dropped Monday, reopened Tuesday as an interim bridge only. It must not appear as a rival end-state option, and must not be left as dropped.
Dmitri abstained ('No view') and later said 'Fine, whatever'. Sofia's 'ok' is a bare acknowledgement. None of the three are support for Databricks.
Raj's and Imani's replies are linked to m040 (Q2). They support Q2, not the platform. Imani's '+1' has no meaning without the reply link.
15% cost reduction was hearsay and was corrected to 10%. The card must show 10% and still mark it second-hand.
$3M was an estimate for the merged workload, not a budget. A card that lists a $3M budget is wrong.
False consensus claim ('all seven'). Correct count: three explicit supporters, two conditional, one abstained then acknowledged, one chair proposing.
Colleen's 'serve notice by Nov 30' is overtaken by the gap Raj raised and Dmitri's extension request. It is not a decision.
Priority order changed. The current order is compliance, cost, speed. The earlier order is superseded.
Two sensitive disclosures. The reason for Imani's absence (health) and the hiring freeze must not appear on the card.
'I'll come back to it' and 'Understood' do not assign on-call to Sofia. The action stays unowned.
Sofia's recap restates the direction and promises a formal confirmation on Nov 16. It is not a recorded group decision.
Off-topic threads (3pm call, parking, expense tool). Separate issues, not blockers.
